assessment.summary: ERBB2 (HER2) is one of the most extensively validated and drugged oncology targets in human medicine, with 14 approved therapeutics including monoclonal antibodies, small-molecule kinase inhibitors, and antibody-drug conjugates. Structural data are outstanding (1.25 Å best resolution, 9 ligand-bound structures), chemical space is deeply explored (>5,000 IC50 entries, median ~300 nM), and the literature base is enormous with continuing active clinical research across multiple tumor types. Druggability is unambiguously high across all evidence dimensions.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 74 with only ~67% high-confidence fraction suggests disordered regions (likely extracellular or linker domains) not fully resolved even in crystal structures — conformational flexibility of certain loops may limit structure-based drug design in those regions

Resistance mechanisms (e.g., ERBB2 mutations, PI3K pathway bypass, HER3 upregulation) are well-documented but not quantified in the evidence provided here, which limits assessment of next-generation drug design opportunities
Median IC50 of ~300 nM across the ChEMBL dataset indicates that many compounds have moderate potency — the distribution of truly sub-nanomolar tool compounds vs. weaker scaffolds is not broken down

Disease indication breadth (bladder, colorectal, liver fibrosis, osteoarthritis in recent titles) suggests expanding biology beyond breast/gastric cancer — full translational validation in non-oncology indications remains incomplete
No explicit data on selectivity profiles or off-target liabilities across the ERBB family (EGFR, HER3, HER4) are summarised here
